problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
-3,\,1,\,-5,\,-5,\,2,\,-8
$$

feedback.problem:
Compute the variance ${\sigma }^{2}$ of the following data set:

$$
1,\,-6,\,-1,\,3,\,-11,\,-4
$$

Do not round your answer.

${\sigma }^{2}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance of the data set is given by 

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ is the mean of the data set.

First, we need to compute the mean. There are $n=6$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (1-6-1+3-11-4) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (-18) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[(1-(-3))^{2}+(-6-(-3))^{2}+(-1-(-3))^{2}+(3-(-3))^{2}+(-11-(-3))^{2}+(-4-(-3))^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[16+9+4+36+64+1] \\  & =\frac{130}{6} \\  & =\frac{65}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
